- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days), especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates prices in the middle to late horizon (days 10–25), particularly when history shows downward momentum.
- Tends to overshoot after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 94.51 → 90.85), then fails to correct downward.
- Shows persistent lag in responding to recent low prices — delays mean reversion by 3–5 days.
- Overconfident in short-term volatility; forecasts often peak too early or too high in volatile periods.
- Underestimates downward trends in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, especially when history shows clear decline.
- Sensitive to recent high values — forecasts often “climb” toward recent peaks rather than adjusting to new context.
- Mean reversion is not strong enough — model holds onto recent highs longer than actual price behavior suggests.
